Morphology defaults

Source: R/rulebook.R
morphology_defaults.Rd

The assumptions behind identifying what each boundary and site is (road frontage, side or rear boundary, corner site, rear site, access leg). Each can be overridden in a rulebook with set_morphology() and again for a single run.

Usage

morphology_defaults()

Value

A named list:

min_road_contact

Shortest total road frontage (m) for a site to count as fronting a road. 0.5.

road_tolerance

Distance (m) within which a boundary counts as running along a road parcel, absorbing cadastral slivers. A boundary segment is a road frontage when at least half its length is within it. 0.5.

boundary_probe_distance

How far (m) across a side or rear boundary to look for the zone opposite. 1.

road_probe_distance

How far (m) across a road boundary to look for the zone opposite, so the probe clears the carriageway. 25.

side_rear_angle_tolerance

Degrees from parallel to the frontage within which a boundary is a rear boundary. 30.

rear_depth_share

How far back (as a share of the site's depth from the frontage) a parallel boundary must sit to be a rear boundary. 0.5.

rear_site_max_frontage

A site with less road frontage than this (m) is a rear site. 7.5.

corner_angle_tolerance

Degrees by which two frontages must differ in bearing for a corner site. 30.

corner_min_frontage

Shortest frontage (m) on each road for a corner site. 3.

through_min_bearing_difference

Degrees between two frontages for a through site. 135.

access_leg_max_width

Widest (m) an access leg (driveway strip of a rear site) may be. 7.5.

access_leg_min_road_contact

Shortest road contact (m) of an access leg. 0.5.

exclude_access_legs

Whether access legs are left out of net site area. TRUE.

boundary_merge_angle

Degrees within which consecutive boundary segments count as one straight boundary. 5.

water_boundary_distance

Distance (m) from a water feature within which a boundary is classed coastal, riparian or lakeside. 20.

reserve_families

Zone families whose land makes a boundary a reserve boundary. "OPEN_SPACE".

min_sliver_area

Pieces of a site (m2) smaller than this, left by a zone boundary, are merged into the larger piece. 1.

access_touch_distance

Distance (m) within which an easement or access lot counts as reaching a rear site (find_access_widths()). 0.5.

access_contact_tolerance

Distance (m) within which a boundary counts as on a road when measuring access width. Small, because cadastral boundaries share surveyed vertices. 0.05.

access_max_strip_width

Road contact wider than this (m) is a lot, not an access strip. 10.

access_lot_max_area

Largest parcel (m2) taken as a possible jointly owned access lot. 800.

front_setback_neighbours

Neighbouring sites on each side whose dwellings set a measured front yard (find_existing_front_setbacks()). 3.

front_setback_min_dwelling_area

Smallest building (m2) counted as a dwelling there, so a garage or shed is not. 50.

front_setback_max_offset

A parcel further than this (m) from the street line is not taken to front it. 60.

rear_site_sides_as_rear

Whether a rear site's side boundaries are rear boundaries, where a plan defines a rear site's yards as all rear yards (Auckland Unitary Plan J1: a rear yard "Includes: all yards on a rear site"). They are tagged rear_site_side. FALSE.

Examples

morphology_defaults()$corner_angle_tolerance
#> [1] 30
